text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Trade union leader Sergio Cofferati said it would be better to bring forward the 1998 budget to summer rather than launch an extra mini-budget now. He added that it was up to the government and not to technicians to reform welfare state (all).

* Prime Minister Romano Prodi in response to newspaper reports, said that a meeting in Rome with the leader of the hard-left Communist Refoundation party Fausto Bertinotti had gone well. But Bertinotti in an interview says that if the extra mini-budget was approved by a different political majority that would bring a government crisis (Corriere della Sera).
* Government parties forced an all-night sitting of the lower house of parliament in response to opposition attempts to block the passage of outstanding 1997 budget measures (all).

* Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said he expected the inflation rate to keep falling from its current level of 2.4 percent. Ciampi also warned that it would be a political error and unbalanced to launch EMU with just a small group of members and that the three percent deficit/GDP target is reachable and sustainable in time for Italy (all).

* Italy's stock exchange ended lower with other stock markets extending losses as US Fed chairman Alan Greenspan warned that the US stock market's rise may be unsustainable. The Mibtel index fell 1.96 percent (all).
* Banca Commerciale italiana posted a stable net profit for 1996 at 341 billion lire from 342.3 billion lire in 1995. Ordinary dividend rose to 165 lire from 150 lire a year before (all).

* Post and Communications minister Antonio Maccanico outlined a package of measures designed to cut telephone bills, including cheaper local and long-distance calls. Trade unions said they were opposed (all).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
